subject: Chemistry
question: In a closed chemical system at Dynamic Chemical Equilibrium, what is true regarding the forward and reverse reaction rates?

options.A: The rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction
options.B: All forward and reverse reactions cease completely
options.C: The concentration of products must exactly equal the concentration of reactants
options.D: The forward reaction proceeds at twice the speed of the reverse reaction

explanation: Dynamic equilibrium is reached when forward and backward reaction rates become equal, keeping macroscopic concentrations constant while microscopic reactions continue.

subject: Chemistry
question: For the reversible gas-phase reaction: $\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g)$, what is the correct equilibrium constant expression ($K_c$)?

options.C: $K_c = \frac{2[\text{NH}_3]}{[\text{N}_2] + 3[\text{H}_2]}$

explanation: By the Law of Mass Action, $K_c$ is the ratio of product concentrations raised to their stoichiometric coefficients over reactant concentrations raised to theirs.

subject: Chemistry
question: If a reversible chemical reaction has an exceptionally large equilibrium constant value (e.g., $K_c = 10^{15}$), this indicates that:

options.A: The reaction proceeds almost to completion and products predominate at equilibrium
options.B: Reactants are overwhelmingly favored and very little product forms
options.C: The reaction cannot take place under any conditions
options.D: The reaction rate is infinitely slow

explanation: A very large $K_c$ ($K_c \gg 1$) indicates that at equilibrium the numerator (products) is vastly larger than the denominator (reactants), meaning near-complete forward conversion.

subject: Chemistry
question: According to Le Chatelier's Principle, what happens to the equilibrium position if additional reactant is continuously added to a system at equilibrium?

options.A: The equilibrium shifts to the right (forward direction) to consume the added reactant
options.B: The equilibrium shifts to the left to produce more reactant
options.C: The equilibrium constant $K_c$ increases permanently
options.D: The total pressure drops to zero

explanation: Le Chatelier's principle states that if a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it adjusts to counteract the disturbance; adding reactant shifts the reaction forward.

subject: Chemistry
question: For the equilibrium $\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g)$ ($4\text{ moles of gas} \rightarrow 2\text{ moles of gas}$), increasing the total external pressure will:

options.A: Shift the equilibrium towards the right (forward direction) producing more Ammonia
options.B: Shift the equilibrium towards the left producing more Nitrogen
options.C: Have no effect on the equilibrium position
options.D: Cause the value of $K_c$ to double

explanation: Increasing pressure favors the direction that produces fewer moles of gas (2 moles of $\text{NH}_3$ vs 4 moles of reactants), shifting the system to the right.

subject: Chemistry
question: For an Exothermic equilibrium reaction ($\Delta H < 0$), increasing the temperature of the system will:

options.A: Shift the equilibrium in the backward (endothermic) direction and decrease $K_c$
options.B: Shift the equilibrium forward and increase $K_c$
options.C: Have no impact on the concentrations

explanation: In an exothermic reaction, heat is a product. Adding heat shifts the equilibrium in the reverse endothermic direction to absorb excess thermal energy, decreasing $K_c$.

subject: Chemistry
question: What effect does adding a catalyst have on the equilibrium position and the value of $K_c$ in a reversible reaction?

options.A: It speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally, reaching equilibrium faster without changing $K_c$
options.B: It shifts the equilibrium forward and increases $K_c$
options.C: It shifts the equilibrium backward and decreases $K_c$
options.D: It prevents equilibrium from ever being attained

explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of both forward and reverse pathways by the same amount; it shortens the time to reach equilibrium without altering equilibrium concentrations or $K_c$.

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following chemical processes is classified as an Irreversible reaction that goes to completion in an open system?

options.A: The combustion of natural gas ($\text{CH}_4 + 2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$)
options.B: Haber process for Ammonia synthesis in a closed reactor
options.C: Contact process for $\text{SO}_3$ formation in a closed tube
options.D: Dissociation of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ into $\text{NO}_2$ in a sealed flask

explanation: Combustion reactions release high energy and gaseous products in an open atmosphere, proceeding unidirectionally to completion with no reverse reaction.

subject: Chemistry
question: What are the units of $K_c$ for the decomposition reaction: $\text{PCl}_5(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3(g) + \text{Cl}_2(g)$?

options.A: $\text{mol} \cdot \text{dm}^{-3}$
options.B: $\text{mol}^{-1} \cdot \text{dm}^3$
options.C: Dimensionless (no units)

explanation: $K_c = \frac{[\text{PCl}_3][\text{Cl}_2]}{[\text{PCl}_5]} = \frac{(\text{mol/dm}^3)(\text{mol/dm}^3)}{\text{mol/dm}^3} = \text{mol} \cdot \text{dm}^{-3}$.

subject: Chemistry
question: The Law of Mass Action, which relates reaction rate to active masses of reactants, was formulated by:

options.A: C.M. Guldberg and Peter Waage (1864)
options.B: Antoine Lavoisier and John Dalton
options.C: Svante Arrhenius and J.H. van 't Hoff

explanation: Norwegian chemists Cato Maximilian Guldberg and Peter Waage proposed the Law of Mass Action in 1864.

subject: Chemistry
question: Formulated in 1864 by Guldberg and Waage, the Law of Mass Action states that the rate of a chemical reaction at any instant is directly proportional to:

options.A: The product of the active masses (molar concentrations) of the reacting substances raised to powers of their stoichiometric coefficients
options.B: The total volume of the reaction vessel
options.C: The total mass of the catalyst
options.D: The surface tension of the solvent

explanation: The law of mass action states: $\text{Rate} \propto [A]^a [B]^b$, where $[A]$ and $[B]$ represent active molar concentrations.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Equilibrium Constant Expression for Ammonia Synthesis
question: For the Haber equilibrium reaction: $\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g)$, what is the correct mathematical expression for the equilibrium constant ($K_c$)?

options.C: $K_c = \frac{2[\text{NH}_3]}{[\text{N}_2] + 3[\text{H}_2]}$

explanation: Products are placed in the numerator and reactants in the denominator, each raised to their stoichiometric powers: $K_c = [\text{NH}_3]^2 / ([\text{N}_2][\text{H}_2]^3)$.

subject: Chemistry
question: For the equilibrium system: $2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g)$ ($3\text{ moles of gas} \rightarrow 2\text{ moles of gas}$), how will increasing the total external pressure shift the equilibrium?

options.A: Shifts to the right (forward direction), toward the side with fewer gas moles ($2\text{ moles of } \text{SO}_3$)
options.B: Shifts to the left (reverse direction)
options.C: Has zero effect on equilibrium composition

explanation: According to Le Chatelier's Principle, increasing pressure shifts the equilibrium in the direction that decreases the total number of gas molecules ($3\text{ mol} \rightarrow 2\text{ mol}$, forward).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Reaction Quotient (Qc) vs Kc Direction Prediction
question: If at a specific point in a reversible reaction the calculated Reaction Quotient is smaller than the Equilibrium Constant ($Q_c < K_c$), how will the system respond to reach equilibrium?

options.A: The reaction will proceed in the forward direction (generating more products) until $Q_c = K_c$
options.B: The reaction will proceed in the reverse direction
options.C: The system is already at dynamic equilibrium
options.D: The value of $K_c$ will decrease to match $Q_c$

explanation: When $Q_c < K_c$, there are fewer products relative to reactants than at equilibrium; the reaction shifts forward to produce more products until $Q_c = K_c$.

subject: Chemistry
question: In the heterogeneous thermal decomposition equilibrium of limestone: $\text{CaCO}_3(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)$, why are solid $\text{CaCO}_3$ and $\text{CaO}$ omitted from the $K_c$ expression?

options.A: The molar concentration (density) of pure solids remains constant and is incorporated into the equilibrium constant ($K_c = [\text{CO}_2]$)
options.B: Solids do not contain chemical bonds
options.C: Carbon dioxide is the only reactant present

explanation: The active mass/concentration of a pure solid depends solely on its density and molar mass, remaining constant during reaction. Thus, $K_c = [\text{CO}_2]$.

subject: Chemistry
question: What are the derived units of $K_c$ for the equilibrium reaction: $\text{H}_2(g) + \text{I}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI}(g)$?

options.A: No units (dimensionless), because the sum of reactant coefficients equals the sum of product coefficients ($\Delta n = 2 - 2 = 0$)
options.B: $\text{mol} \cdot \text{dm}^{-3}$
options.C: $\text{mol}^{-1} \cdot \text{dm}^3$

explanation: Units of $K_c = (\text{mol/dm}^3)^{\Delta n}$. Here $\Delta n = 2 - (1+1) = 0$; $(\text{mol/dm}^3)^0 = 1$ (no units).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Effect of Catalyst on Equilibrium Position
question: What is the exact effect of adding a finely divided Iron catalyst to the Haber Ammonia equilibrium system?

options.A: It increases the rates of both forward and reverse reactions equally, reaching equilibrium faster without changing the equilibrium yield or $K_c$
options.B: It increases the net percentage yield of ammonia by $50\%$
options.C: It shifts the equilibrium completely to the reactants side
options.D: It doubles the numerical value of $K_c$

explanation: A catalyst speeds up attainment of equilibrium by lowering activation energy for both directions equally; it does NOT alter the equilibrium concentrations, yield, or $K_c$.

subject: Chemistry
question: If a reversible chemical reaction has an extremely small equilibrium constant ($K_c = 10^{-15}$), this indicates that at equilibrium:

options.A: Reactants are overwhelmingly favored and only negligible trace amounts of products are formed
options.B: The reaction goes virtually to $100\%$ completion
options.C: Forward reaction rate is infinite

explanation: A very small $K_c \ll 1$ signifies that very little product is present at equilibrium, indicating the forward reaction occurs to a negligible extent.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Le Chatelier's Principle - Temperature Effect on Endothermic System
question: For an endothermic reversible reaction ($\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g) + \text{Heat} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_2(g), \Delta H > 0$), what will be observed when the reaction vessel is heated?

options.A: The equilibrium shifts forward, increasing the concentration of dark reddish-brown $\text{NO}_2$ gas and increasing $K_c$
options.B: The equilibrium shifts reverse, making the mixture colorless
options.C: The total pressure drops to zero

explanation: For an endothermic reaction, heat acts as a reactant. Supplying heat shifts the equilibrium forward to absorb excess thermal energy, producing more brown $\text{NO}_2$ and increasing $K_c$.

subject: Chemistry
question: Why is chemical equilibrium termed 'Dynamic' rather than 'Static'?

options.A: Forward and reverse chemical reactions continue to occur simultaneously at identical microscopic rates ($r_f = r_r$)
options.B: All molecular motion halts completely at equilibrium
options.C: The reaction vessel continuously moves across the laboratory
options.D: Reactants are continuously destroyed into energy

explanation: Dynamic equilibrium is an active balance where opposing forward and reverse processes continue at equal rates, keeping macroscopic concentrations invariant.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Equilibrium Constant Expression for Heterogeneous Equilibria
question: For the heterogeneous thermal decomposition equilibrium $\text{CaCO}_3(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)$, what is the correct equilibrium constant expression ($K_c$)?

options.A: $K_c = [\text{CO}_2]$ (pure solids have constant activity $= 1$)
options.B: $K_c = \frac{[\text{CaO}][\text{CO}_2]}{[\text{CaCO}_3]}$
options.C: $K_c = [\text{CaO}][\text{CO}_2]$

explanation: In heterogeneous equilibria, the concentrations of pure solid phases ($\ext{CaCO}_3, \ext{CaO}$) are constant and incorporated into the equilibrium constant: $K_c = [\ext{CO}_2]$ (or $K_p = P_{\ext{CO}_2}$).

subject: Chemistry
question: If at a particular moment in a reacting mixture the Reaction Quotient ($Q_c$) is less than the Equilibrium Constant ($Q_c < K_c$), the system will:

options.A: Shift in the forward direction (left to right) to convert more reactants into products until $Q_c = K_c$
options.B: Shift in the reverse direction
options.C: Remain in dynamic equilibrium

explanation: When $Q_c < K_c$, product concentrations are lower than required for equilibrium. The reaction proceeds forward to increase products until $Q_c = K_c$.

subject: Chemistry
question: In the industrial synthesis of Ammonia ($\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3, \Delta H = -92\text{ kJ/mol}$), why is an optimum compromise temperature of $450^\circ\text{C}$ used rather than room temperature?

options.A: To achieve an economically viable reaction rate while maintaining an acceptable equilibrium yield in the presence of an Iron catalyst
options.B: Because the reaction is impossible below $400^\circ\text{C}$
options.C: To prevent iron catalyst from turning into gold
options.D: To freeze the ammonia into solid blocks

explanation: Although lower temperature thermodynamically favors exothermic ammonia yield, the kinetic rate is too slow. $450^\circ\text{C}$ with iron catalyst balances rate and yield.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Effect of Adding an Inert Gas at Constant Volume
question: If an inert noble gas (such as Argon) is pumped into an equilibrium system ($2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3$) at Constant Volume, what is the effect on the equilibrium position?

options.A: No effect on equilibrium position because partial pressures and molar concentrations of reacting gases remain unchanged
options.B: Shifts forward
options.C: Shifts backward

explanation: Adding an inert gas at constant volume increases total pressure, but does not alter partial pressures or concentrations of reactants/products; hence equilibrium position is unaffected.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Contact Process for Sulfuric Acid Catalyst
question: In the Contact Process, the catalytic oxidation of sulfur dioxide ($2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3$) uses which industrial catalyst at $450^\circ\text{C}$?

options.A: Vanadium(V) Oxide ($\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$)
options.B: Nickel metal
options.C: Aluminium powder

explanation: Vanadium pentoxide ($\ext{V}_2\ext{O}_5$) provides an active surface at $450^circ\ext{C}$ to catalyze the conversion of $\ext{SO}_2$ to $\ext{SO}_3$ in the manufacture of sulfuric acid.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Equilibrium Constant Units for Equal Moles
question: For the esterification equilibrium $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{COOC}_2\text{H}_5 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$, what are the units of $K_c$?

options.A: Dimensionless / No units (since $\Delta n = 2 - 2 = 0$)
options.B: $\text{mol}\cdot\text{dm}^{-3}$
options.C: $\text{mol}^2\cdot\text{dm}^{-6}$

explanation: When total moles of gaseous/aqueous products equal total moles of reactants ($\Delta n = 0$), concentration units cancel out completely, making $K_c$ dimensionless.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Magnitude of Kc and Extent of Reaction
question: If a reversible chemical reaction has an extremely large equilibrium constant ($K_c = 10^{20}$), this quantitatively indicates that:

options.A: The reaction proceeds almost to completion, with products vastly dominating at equilibrium
options.B: Practically no reaction occurs
options.C: Reactants and products are present in exact 50:50 equal amounts

explanation: A very large $K_c \gg 1$ indicates that the numerator (products) is enormous compared to denominator (reactants), meaning the forward reaction goes virtually to completion.

subject: Chemistry
question: Why is chemical equilibrium classified as 'Dynamic' rather than 'Static'?

options.A: Forward and reverse reactions continue to occur simultaneously at exactly identical rates ($r_f = r_r$), so macroscopic concentrations remain constant
options.B: All chemical molecules freeze into rigid crystals
options.C: The reaction container rotates dynamically in space

explanation: Chemical equilibrium is dynamic because molecular collisions and transformations never stop; microscopic forward and backward rates are equal, creating constant macroscopic state.

subject: Chemistry
question: According to van 't Hoff's relationship, for an Endothermic reaction ($\Delta H > 0$), what happens to the value of $K_c$ when the temperature is raised?

options.A: $K_c$ increases
options.B: $K_c$ decreases
options.C: $K_c$ remains strictly unchanged

explanation: In endothermic reactions, heat acts like a reactant. Increasing temperature shifts equilibrium forward to absorb heat, increasing product concentrations and raising $K_c$.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Le Chatelier's Principle - N2O4 and NO2 Equilibrium
question: In the gaseous equilibrium $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4\text{ (colorless)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_2\text{ (brown)}, \Delta H = +57\text{ kJ/mol}$, placing the sealed tube in an ice bath will:

options.A: Turn the mixture lighter / colorless as equilibrium shifts to the exothermic reverse direction forming $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$
options.B: Turn the mixture intensely dark brown
options.C: Cause the glass tube to explode from pressure

explanation: Cooling an endothermic forward reaction shifts equilibrium in the reverse exothermic direction according to Le Chatelier's principle, forming colorless $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$.
